summary: The root entry keeps the related spellings מֵחַ and מֹחַ together. מֵחַ is a fattened animal used in offerings, while מֹחַ is marrow inside bones. מַחְמָאוֹת belongs to חמאה and is excluded.

senses.definition: A fatling is a fattened animal offered to Yahweh with the sacrifice.
Marrow is the rich substance within bones, described as moistening them.
The plural names fattened animals, following מֵחַ.

note: מַחְמָאוֹת (m.bn.ay) means flattering words and belongs under חמאה, not מחח. Zero-token מֵחַ m.bj.ai and מָחָה m.bm.ac are cross-references.
